headline: Dry through Wednesday morning, then a weak front, with a stronger, windier storm series starting Friday and continuing into next week.
summary: As of Tuesday evening, dry weather continues into Wednesday morning. A weak front arrives Wednesday evening into Thursday with lowland rain and locally breezy winds from around Whidbey Island northward. Thursday afternoon should be mostly dry in the lowlands, with rain or drizzle lingering in the mountains, and highs in the mid to upper 50s through Thursday. The weather turns more active Friday as a string of fronts (the leading edges of storm systems) crosses western Washington. The first brings rain and gusty south winds, strongest along the immediate coast and from Admiralty Inlet northward, where forecasters give 40 to 80% odds of gusts over 40 mph and are watching whether a wind alert will be needed. A warm front on Saturday keeps rain going at times on the Olympic Peninsula and near the Canadian border, with a brief drier spell for some of Puget Sound. A cold front follows Saturday night into Sunday with more rain and breezy winds. Because many trees still have leaves, localized power outages are possible over the weekend. Snow levels stay high, mainly 5000 to 8000 feet from Friday into Sunday, so snow is limited to high elevations. Seas near the coast build toward 15 to 20 feet on Friday, and forecasters are watching for high surf. Ensemble forecasts (sets of computer model runs) suggest a brief break in the heavier precipitation Sunday night into Monday, then another front late Monday and a continued active pattern next week; that timing is uncertain. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect for land areas, and river flooding is not expected in the next seven days, though repeated rain will start to soak the ground and raise river flows.
changes: Early-day discussions expected a wetter, windier Wednesday, with the strongest storm Thursday night into Friday. By afternoon, forecasters described Wednesday as dry until a weak front that evening and shifted the stronger storm's start to Friday. They also added the power outage risk from leafy trees and raised the Friday wind odds to as high as 80%.
